why: A only grades races that had trades and repeats grades already shown under each decision; the owner wants a verdict on the report card itself. B judges what a report card is for: is the self-grade honest given what happened, is the explanation right, is the plan for tomorrow sensible.
rubric: (1) honesty: does the self-grade match the day's result and the quality of the decisions? (2) accuracy: are the facts and numbers in the write-up right? (3) the plan: specific, sensible, consistent with the race's rules. A excellent, B good, C acceptable, D poor, F misleading; or no view. One sentence, 20 words or fewer.
details: Same anonymity (Competitor A/B, reshuffled), same strict tone, same 'never changes a score'. Results ARE shown to the grader here, because judging a review needs them. Gemini and ChatGPT grade in their first check-in after the day closes; Claude grades in its daily session. Grade every race of every report card, All in included, back to Day 1.
display: On each line of the report card: the self-grade, then 'Gemini's view C' and 'ChatGPT's view B' (each a small chip; tap for the sentence), labelled as competitors' opinions.
